newsitem.title: USA: Eight ADM board members to step down.
newsitem.headline: Eight ADM board members to step down.

text.p: Eight members of Archer Daniels Midland Co's board of directors will not stand for re-election at this year's annual meeting in October, including two former executives and four current executives.
In its proxy statement, ADM outlined 12 nominees to the board, which has been scaled back from 17 members originally. Of the 12 nominees, nine are current board members.
The composition of the board has come under scrutiny as several institutional shareholders have pressed for more independent directors on ADM's board.

Among those stepping down this year are John H. Daniels, retired chairman, and Ralph Bruce, retired executive vice president. Also retiring from the board are two outside directors, Ray Goldberg, a Harvard University professor, and Mrs. Nelson Rockefeller, the proxy statement said.

These four directors were among the board members who had been expected to step down as part of ADM's new rules for its directors, which set an age limit of 70 for new directors. However, directors who already reached that age were not obliged to leave the board.

As previously announced, H.D. Hale, chairman of ADM Milling Co; Michael Andreas, vice chairman and executive vice president; Martin Andreas, senior vice president, and James Randall, president; are not standing for reelection to make way for more independent directors on the board.
According to the proxy, Chairman Dwayne Andreas will be the only current company executive on the board.

New board nominees include John Block, former U.S. Secretary of Agriculture; Richard Burt, former Ambassador to Germany and a Washington consultant; and Mollie Hale Carter, a senior investment officer for John Hancock Mutual Life.

In addition to Dwayne Andreas, current board members who are standing for reelection include Lowell Andreas, retired ADM president; Gaylord Coan, president of Gold Kist Inc ; Shreve Archer Jr., a private investor; John Vanier, chief executive officer of Western Star Ag Resources Inc ; M. Brian Mulroney, former Canadian Prime Minister and a senior partner at Ogilvy Renault law firm; O. Glenn Webb, chairman of GROWMARK Inc cooperative; F. Ross Johnson, chairman of RJM Group Inc, and Robert Strauss, former ambassador to Russia and a partner in the law firm of Akin, Gkump, Strauss, Hauer & Feld.

As previously reported, two institutional shareholders, the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund and the California Public Employees' Retirement System, have submitted a proposal that defines what they consider to be independent board members.
Under the proposed definition, an independent board member has not been employed by the company for five years and has no business or personal connection with ADM and executives.
